result.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
result.summary: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact counts in an open pretraining corpus show. In real-time nowcasts, every lookahead premium we estimate on US GDP is smaller than the forecast comparison can detect at macroeconomic sample sizes, and none on GDP or inflation survives correction for multiple testing. Lookahead audits should therefore measure memory directly against memory-free models on the same items.

AI.brief_summary: 论文测量语言模型阅读央行文件（FOMC 声明与纪要）时的「时间污染」：模型预训练语料晚于所读文件，可能凭记忆而非阅读答题；作者以只训练固定日期前文本的时序一致模型作对照，在同批问题上量化记忆贡献，并发现 GDP 与通胀预测的前视溢价在宏观样本量下不可检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「与无记忆模型在同一题目上对比、且不以随机为基线」的审计思路，可能为 LVR 中判断答案究竟来自 latent 视觉证据还是语言/任务先验提供评价线索；但该文属纯文本经济预测，与视觉推理机制无直接联系，可迁移性需核查。
